summary: Monks Hill fire tower, Kingston MA: first tower 1916, present steel tower 1956, Register entry 2004; grounds are Town of Kingston land (Camp Nekon).

corrections.why: 9.1 m is 30 feet, the figure for the 1916 tower in the Forest Lookouts quote; the present steel tower is 75 feet (about 22.9 m) per the Register

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Register and the FFLA post give 38 ft; the Forest Lookouts page quotes a 1916 state report giving 30 ft. The register figure is used and the 30 ft figure is noted.
The Register gives 75 ft; the FFLA post gives 68 ft. The register figure is used and the 68 ft figure is noted.
The Register says both towers were kept in service; the Forest Lookouts page quotes a 1916 state report saying the Plymouth tower would be retained as a drought substation.

The FFLA post says the site was briefly abandoned from the late 1930s to mid 1940s, yet a Town of Kingston historical sketch describes residents keeping watch from Monk Tower from December 1941 to January 1943, to watch Kingston Bay for suspicious activity. The sketch does not call that a fire watch, so the two accounts are not reconciled.

notes_for_editor: Built and replacement dates are well sourced, but the register dates the present tower to 1956 while the FFLA post's height (68 ft) differs from the register (75 ft). No source read gives current condition or staffing after 1945; the 2004 register entry is the latest tower-specific record. The 2017 FFLA post was readable and is cited for the 1916 height, the abandonment, and the 68 ft figure. The Town sketch gives the logbook watch's purpose as watching Kingston Bay for suspicious activity and does not call it a fire watch, so whether the WWII watch relates to the fire tower is undocumented. Camp Nekon is town conservation land; whether the tower is open for climbing is undocumented.
